subject: research/swe-backfill
professional: an empirical software-engineering researcher in mining software repositories (MSR). They would check first how bug-fix commits are identified (keyword heuristics in the style of Mockus and Votta 2000, SZZ of Sliwerski, Zimmermann and Zeller 2005) and whether the keyword classifier was hand-validated for false positives (Herzig, Just and Zeller 2013), how renames and parallel-branch history are handled (Bird et al. 2009, 'The promises and perils of mining git'), and whether the extract is pinned to a recorded ref so it can be reproduced

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py` (python3.13): output byte-identical to experiments/results.txt. Recomputed every headline from commits.jsonl with my own code that imports nothing from the subject (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a970c956-8347-5ada-9f27-66faff8c126b/scratchpad/swe/re.py): 517 commits, 396 slugs, per-day creations 1/89/129/20/93/61/3, median creation gap 4.2 min, 275 of 395 gaps <=10 min, never-touched 302/396, observed n 234 with 6 correction-worded hits, era split 239 early (22 logged) / 157 late (157 logged), the same 5 log-only slugs, Wilson 6/234 = 0.0118 to 0.0548 and 302/396 = 0.718 to 0.802 by solving the score quadratic directly: all match. Checked the extract against a source the author did not write, the GitHub API: commits ddb362fdc3c (2026-09-28T16:50:47Z, 'Add peer-prediction verification markets research package', 15 files added under research/decentralized-verification-markets of which 5 are test_*.py), 019565f1a2f (2026-09-29T04:20:01Z, 2 files modified under effort-elicitation) and c084c28a8c8 (2026-10-13T02:19:49Z, rename) match time, subject and counts; list_commits path=research for 2026-10-02..10-12 returns [] so the quiet window is real upstream. But hand-reading the 6 'correction' hits shows one false positive: eiv-twin's 556272fb434 'Add eiv-twin: ... 1/lambda controller overshoot, and repair costs' is the completion of a WIP creation, matched on the domain word 'repair'. The headline 6/234 (2.6%) presented as a lower bound is 5/234 (2.1%); removing 'repair' from FIX_RE reproduces 5/234. extract.py also attributes the source side of a rename to the old slug as 'M' (5 rename commits, e.g. c084c28a8c8 records chip-rtl-loop M=57), adding spurious later touches to the projects whose slug was taken. Wrong number is small and inside the interval, so 2, not 1.
evidence.completeness: Claimed deliverables: the extract (commits.jsonl, 517 lines, present), 9 tests (ran: 'Ran 9 tests in 0.008s OK'), run.py reproducing results.txt (identical), the per-day figure (projects_per_day.svg present), the run-log comparison (runs ../swe-ledger snapshot, present). extract.py cannot be rerun here (shallow clone) and the ref/commit it was run against is not recorded; the extract ends at 2026-10-15T03:28:56Z although GitHub lists 100+ research commits on 2026-10-15. The README is explicit about what it does not do (tokens, PRs, CI). Everything it says is done works end to end.
evidence.verification: `cd research/swe-backfill && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 9 tests OK. Seeded 5 mutations in src/swe_backfill/backfill.py with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, each reverted with git checkout: censoring cutoff end -> end+1 day (headline observed n 234 -> 239), close-pair '<=' -> '<', creation rule 'A > 0' -> 'A >= 0', drop 'repair' from FIX_RE (headline 6 -> 5), removed-flag always on D (removed 1 -> 2). All 5 survived: 0/5 caught, including two that change a README headline. Tests use hand-made fixtures and pin no number from the real extract.
evidence.craft: Read backfill.py (170 lines), run.py, extract.py, tests. Small, readable, standard library only. Defects: extract.py:271 classifies the source path of an 'R' entry as 'M' instead of 'D' (renames count as edits of the old slug, and the 'removed' flag can never fire for a rename); the git ref and HEAD used for the extract are not written to the output; FIX_RE is a bare keyword list with no word-context guard; run.py and tests use 'from ... import *'; run.py silently skips the whole run-log section when the sibling snapshot is missing (backs two README headlines).
evidence.claims: Checked: 517/396/span (results.txt:1, pass); per-day burst and 10-02..10-12 gap (pass, and confirmed upstream via GitHub API); 157/157 late in log and 22/239 early (pass); 49% in families (pass); 152 close pairs (pass); 6/234 lower bound (fail: includes a false positive, 5/234); 'Family members and other projects look alike (4/196 and 4/200)' is placed in the observed-window paragraph but is computed over all projects incl. censored (partial); 'This data cannot tell them apart' (duplicate claim vs deliberate series) is contradicted by the data: 5 commit subjects in commits.jsonl say the slug was taken by a parallel run ('Rename to chip-rtl-probe: slug chip-rtl-loop landed in parallel', 'Rename to robofab-cell-bound: robofab-cell slug merged first from a parallel run', etc.) (fail); 'every commit ... from the full history' with no recorded ref, ending 03:28 on 10-15 (partial). Limits section is honest and specific; AI-assistance disclosure present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher on track 10 can build on it, and three later projects do (research/swe-prflow, swe-spendoutput, swe-reccover cite it). The extract and history reader are reusable. But it is a descriptive count, not a result: no hypothesis, no validated defect measure, and the one correctness proxy is uncalibrated. Nearest prior work (MSR bug-fix mining: Mockus and Votta 2000; SZZ, Sliwerski et al. 2005; Herzig et al. 2013 on misclassification; Bird et al. 2009 on git-mining perils) is not cited, so a reader is not told the keyword proxy has known 30%+ misclassification rates in the literature. Novelty: none claimed beyond this repository, appropriately.
evidence.domain: Against MSR practice: keyword-based fix detection without a hand-validated sample (6 hits would take minutes; 1 of 6 is wrong); no rename/copy detection policy stated (git log default rename detection is on, and the old path is mis-bucketed); author time used for ordering with parallel branches merged non-linearly (acknowledged in Limitations); the extract is not pinned to a commit. Wilson intervals and the explicit censoring of the 14-day window are correct and good practice. A senior MSR reviewer would ask for the validated sample and the rename fix before signing off.

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible descriptive study: run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte, every headline count recomputes from the extract with independent code, and three commits plus the 10-02..10-12 quiet window check out against the GitHub API. It does not meet the bar. The one correctness proxy it reports, a 'lower bound' of 6/234 correction-worded follow-ups, contains a false positive (eiv-twin's 'repair costs'), so the true count is 5/234; the keyword list was never hand-checked although there were only six hits. Its own data holds 5 commits stating a slug was taken by a parallel run, which contradicts the README's 'this data cannot tell them apart'. Tests caught 0 of 5 seeded mutations, two of which move README headlines. Renames are mis-bucketed in extract.py, the extract ref is not recorded, and MSR prior work on fix-commit mining is not cited.
